quizzes.stem: Scenario: Larch Mutual's assistant answers a coverage question with a limit of 3,000, and the current policy says 5,000. Latency and the model version have not changed since the documents were refreshed. Where does the investigation start?

options.a: The retrieval step, to see whether a stale chunk was returned
options.b: The system prompt, to see whether its wording on limits was changed
options.c: The sampling temperature, to see whether it was lowered by a release
options.d: The context window, to see whether the prompt was cut short

explanation.a: A confident wrong answer after a refresh points to stale evidence.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page rejects "Fix the wrong answer in the prompt" as a first move, since a wrong answer after a document refresh points to the evidence before the wording.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page says to "check the version of the evidence before the model", and a temperature change would not return the exact old figure.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the stale index holds the chunk "Water damage is covered up to 3,000 per claim.", the very figure the assistant gave, which a cut-short prompt would not produce.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: A change to the retrieval step gains three answers in a minor segment and loses one in the segment where an error costs 250. The totals favour the change. What does the gate return, and why?

options.a: Release it, because the gains outnumber the losses
options.b: Release it, because the owner can review the lost case later
options.c: Refuse it, because the lost case falls in a guarded area
options.d: Refuse it, because any lost answer outweighs the gains

explanation.c: The segment where an error costs 250 is the one the gate protects, and a loss there is a veto whatever the gains.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a loss in a protected segment is a veto whatever the gains elsewhere".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the gate does not leave the lost case to a later review: it "says no-go and names the segment".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the gate's rule is that "the losses do not outnumber the gains" for a loss outside a protected segment, so such a loss does not outweigh the gains on its own.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: A review of a pilot finds one medium finding, a missing owner, and two low findings, a small evaluation set and an unstated accuracy. There is no high finding. What does the review conclude?

options.a: Approve it, since no finding is serious enough to stop the pilot
options.b: Revise it, since its worst flaw weakens but does not block it
options.c: Reject it, since three findings together are too many to approve
options.d: Approve it, since two of its three findings are only low ones

explanation.b: With no high finding and a medium one, the review asks for a revision.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "revise if none is high and any is medium", so a medium finding stops an approval.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A fixed ladder keeps a pile of small findings from becoming a rejection", and a rejection needs a high finding, which is absent.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the ladder approves "a design with only low findings", and this one also has a medium finding.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: A reviewer proposes to write the findings grouped by domain, P1 first, because the course is organised in that order. What is the objection?

options.a: The sponsor would have to read every finding to reach the verdict
options.b: Two reviewers would still produce different lists from the same design
options.c: A finding that spans two domains would be listed twice in the review
options.d: A flaw that rejects could sit below flaws that only ask for revision

explanation.d: A list ordered only by domain puts severity second, so a high finding in a later domain falls below milder ones in earlier domains.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the review is written with "the verdict first, then the scorecard, then the findings in their order", so the sponsor reaches the verdict before any finding.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Two reviewers must produce the same list", and a fixed order by domain and rule id also gives the same list.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Each finding is a severity, a domain and a rule", so a finding sits under one domain and is listed once.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: A proposal uses a team of agents for a task whose steps are known in advance and whose value equals ten chats. The designer says the team is more flexible. What does the review record?

options.a: One medium and one low item under P1, so it goes back for revision
options.b: One high item under P1 for the team's cost, so it is rejected
options.c: Two medium items under P1, so the plan goes back for revision
options.d: Two low items under P1, so it is approved with both recorded

explanation.c: The path is known, so the team is unneeded, and a value of ten is below fifteen, which makes two medium rules fire.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the table lists "a team's value is below 15 chats' worth" as medium, like the known-path rule, so neither item is low.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "reject if any finding is high", and neither rule is high.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the rule table lists "an agent or a team is used where the path is known" as medium and not low.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: A review is run on two proposals that differ in one number: the first has an evaluation set of 20 cases and the second has 19. What does the review record for each?

options.a: Both are flagged, and the thinner suite more severely
options.b: Only the thinner suite is flagged, with a low item under P4
options.c: Neither is flagged, since one case short is within the tolerance
options.d: Both are flagged, each with the same low item under P4

explanation.b: The edge is met at 20 and missed at 19, and the rule is low.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "an evaluation set of exactly 20 cases passes", so the fuller suite is not flagged, and the table lists the rule as low for "fewer than 20 evaluation cases", whatever the shortfall.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "One step past any of them is a finding".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "an evaluation set of exactly 20 cases passes", so the fuller suite has no finding.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: A pipeline sends customer email addresses to the model in the prompt, and the audit log stores every prompt. Which description of the result fits?

options.a: Two blocking items, each enough on its own to reject it
options.b: Two items that ask for revision and nothing that blocks
options.c: One minor item that is only recorded and one that blocks
options.d: One blocking item and one revision item, with none minor

explanation.d: Identifiers reaching the model is high and the audit log keeping content is medium, both in P5.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the table lists "the audit log stores content" as medium, which asks for revision.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the table lists "identifiers go to the model" as high, which blocks.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the low bullet reads "It is recorded and does not hold the design back", and neither flaw is low.
